newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast diesel prices firm on refinery news.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast diesel prices firm on refinery news.

text.p: U.S. West Coast CARB diesel prices firmed midday Monday, following a Friday might explosion at Paramount's Los Angeles-area refinery.
The explosion occured in jet fuel heat exchanger, according to fire officials.
Traders said the damaged equipment would disrupt diesel production from the hydrotreating unit, and cause cutbacks in conventional gasoline production.
But most traders shrugged off a long-term impact, since the refinery processes a small 30,000 barrel-per-day of crude.
CARB diesel were offered as high as 90 cents a gallon, a two cent jump from Friday. Bids were heard around 87/88 cents a gallon, a slight rise from late last week.
"EPA," or low sulphur diesel traded thinly, and gained about a cent to 76/77 cents.
Jet fuel prices, which posted a steady rise last week, fell two cents Monday, as cargoes began arriving to the West Coast from the U.S. Gulf.
Conventional gasoline prices in Los Angeles and San Francisco rose slightly to 76/76.50 cents a gallon on news of the damaged Paramount plant.
CARB gasoline was offered at 81 cents a gallon in L.A. and two cents weaker in San Francisco, unchanged on a slow news day.
